claims.claim: food at zero somatic growth 64 and 104 µg C/L (P-sufficient); 127 and 311 (C:P 1,200); D. magna, Scenedesmus, 20 °C
claims.location: p. 2555 (PDF p. 4), Results; p. 2556 (PDF p. 5), Table 1
claims.quote: experiments (64 µg C/L, 104 µg C/L) than those in the low-P treatments (127
claims.conditions: laboratory flow-through vessels (120 mL, 1 L/d), 20 °C, dim light; 1-d-old D. magna neonates (5 per vessel, 3 replicates) grown 3 d on Scenedesmus obliquus at 30–150 µg C/L; algal C:P 200 (high-P) vs 1200 (low-P); thresholds from linear regressions of somatic growth on food. Experiment 1: neonates from well-fed mothers; experiment 2: born in food-free medium (lower reserves)
claims.note: 95 % intervals: 54–76, 86–115 (P-sufficient); 99–252 and 195–undefined (P-limited). Adding phosphate to the P-limited algae just before feeding brought the threshold back to 65 and 95 µg C/L

claims.claim: Daphnia stop growing at 0.06–0.10 mg C/L of good food (Boersma & Kreutzer 2002)
claims.conditions: as above: laboratory, D. magna neonates, 3-d growth, 20 °C, P-sufficient S. obliquus
claims.note: 0.064–0.104 mg C/L; neonate somatic growth, not a population's zero-growth food

claims.claim: the food at which a Daphnia stops growing is 0.03–0.1 mg C/L in the field (Lampert 1977, Boersma & Kreutzer 2002)
claims.source_value: laboratory, not field: 0.064 and 0.104 mg C/L for D. magna neonates on P-sufficient Scenedesmus obliquus (20 °C, 3-d growth), 0.127 and 0.311 on P-limited algae (C:P 1200)
claims.location: p. 2554 (PDF p. 3), Methods; p. 2556 (PDF p. 5), Table 1
claims.quote: C:P ratios for high-phosphorus (200) and low-phosphorus (1200) algae were constant
claims.note: Boersma & Kreutzer supply the 0.06–0.10 part of the range, measured in the laboratory; the 0.03 lower end must come from Lampert 1977 (not read here). On P-limited food, the kind the Hot Brook model's seston represents, their thresholds were 2–3× higher

notes: Also useful: starving neonates lost mass at −0.096 d⁻¹ (pre-fed) and −0.170 d⁻¹ (born without food) over 3 d at 20 °C. Mothers on low-P food were half the dry mass of those on high-P (275 vs 526 µg; Table 2); their neonates had the same mass but more lipid and less P, and grew better on P-limited food.
